introduction.summary: This specification records the project purpose, stakeholder constraints and unresolved decisions stated in the source evidence below.

items.title: Stakeholder source statement E-001
items.detail: Design a secure email security gateway for a university that protects students, faculty, staff, and administrators from phishing, malicious attachments, spoofed messages, and suspicious links.

items.title: Stakeholder source statement E-002
items.detail: The system should inspect incoming and outgoing email traffic, detect suspicious messages, quarantine potentially harmful emails, generate security alerts, and allow authorized administrators to review and release quarantined messages.

items.title: Stakeholder source statement E-003
items.detail: The platform should maintain audit logs of filtering decisions and administrator actions, integrate with the university identity system, and provide a dashboard for monitoring email security events.

items.title: Stakeholder source statement E-004
items.detail: The solution should be secure, reliable, scalable, and manageable for university-wide deployment.

functional.applicability_reason: Source-backed obligations; unspecified decisions remain open.

requirements.title: inspect incoming and outgoing email traffic for phishing attempts, malicious attachments, spoofed messages, and suspicious links.
requirements.statement: The system shall inspect incoming and outgoing email traffic for phishing attempts, malicious attachments, spoofed messages, and suspicious links.

acceptance_criteria.given: An email with a malicious attachment is sent to a university user
acceptance_criteria.when: The email security gateway processes the message during transmission
acceptance_criteria.then: The system detects the malicious content and quarantines the message
acceptance_criteria.observable_evidence: Test capture of the quarantine action triggered by the gateway

acceptance_criteria.given: A spoofed message is received from an external sender
acceptance_criteria.when: The message arrives at the university's email server
acceptance_criteria.then: The system identifies the spoofing attempt and generates a security alert for administrators
acceptance_criteria.observable_evidence: Test capture of the generated security alert

unresolved_decisions: Thresholds for what constitutes a suspicious link or attachment are not defined

requirements.title: allow authorized administrators to review quarantined messages and release them if deemed safe.
requirements.statement: The system shall allow authorized administrators to review quarantined messages and release them if deemed safe.

acceptance_criteria.given: An administrator requests access to a quarantined message
acceptance_criteria.when: The request is processed by the email security gateway
acceptance_criteria.then: The administrator receives the message for review and can approve or reject it
acceptance_criteria.observable_evidence: Test capture of the approval workflow for a quarantined message

acceptance_criteria.given: A message is released after administrative review
acceptance_criteria.when: It is delivered to the recipient's inbox
acceptance_criteria.observable_evidence: Test capture of successful message delivery post-release

unresolved_decisions: Access controls for which administrators can approve messages are not defined

nonfunctional.applicability_reason: Source-backed obligations; unspecified decisions remain open.

requirements.title: The solution shall be secure, reliable, scalable, and manageable for university-wide deployment.
requirements.statement: The solution shall be secure, reliable, scalable, and manageable for university-wide deployment.

acceptance_criteria.given: A university administrator initiates a deployment request for the system across campus networks
acceptance_criteria.when: The system is configured to operate in a university-wide environment
acceptance_criteria.then: The system remains secure, reliable, scalable, and manageable under operational conditions
acceptance_criteria.observable_evidence: Test capture of system behavior during university-wide deployment

unresolved_decisions: Definition of scalability in terms of message volume or user count
Criteria for reliability under network failure or high load
Specifics of manageability including interface usability and access controls

security.applicability_reason: Source-backed obligations; unspecified decisions remain open.

requirements.title: The platform shall maintain audit logs of filtering decisions and administrator actions, integrate with the university identity system, and provide a dashboard for monitoring email security events.
requirements.statement: The platform shall maintain audit logs of filtering decisions and administrator actions, integrate with the university identity system, and provide a dashboard for monitoring email security events.

acceptance_criteria.given: An administrator performs a filtering action or reviews quarantined messages
acceptance_criteria.when: The system processes the request and records the decision
acceptance_criteria.then: A log entry is generated in the platform's audit database indicating the action type, timestamp, user ID, and message details
acceptance_criteria.observable_evidence: Test capture of the audit log record after a filtering action or quarantine review

acceptance_criteria.given: An operator accesses the email security dashboard via the university identity system
acceptance_criteria.when: The operator views real-time monitoring events and alerts
acceptance_criteria.then: The dashboard displays current threats, event counts, and administrator actions with accurate timestamps
acceptance_criteria.observable_evidence: Test capture of the dashboard interface showing live threat data

unresolved_decisions: Whether audit logs shall be retained for 30 days or longer
How real-time monitoring thresholds are defined

data.applicability_reason: Existing canonical requirements, where applicable, are linked below; this section adds no separate obligation. Unresolved stakeholder decisions remain open.

network.applicability_reason: Existing canonical requirements, where applicable, are linked below; this section adds no separate obligation. Unresolved stakeholder decisions remain open.

open_decisions: Which specific identity-based authentication mechanisms (e.g., MFA, device fingerprinting) should be implemented for email access in the university environment?
How will dynamic risk-based policies be defined and evaluated to determine whether a user should be allowed to access sensitive data or perform high-risk actions?
What thresholds will trigger quarantining of messages or generation of security alerts?
How will real-time monitoring of device health, patch levels, and network traffic be implemented for email endpoints?
Will the system use certificate-based device identity or other forms of device authentication?
How will access to sensitive data (e.g., payroll) be controlled based on user behavior and location?
What is the definition of 'scalability' in terms of message volume or number of users, and how will it be measured during deployment?
What are the specific reliability criteria under network failure or high load conditions?
How will manageability be ensured through interface usability, access controls, and operational workflows?

items.title: Log
items.detail: A collection of event records. This term does not itself require additional logging fields, events or access permissions.

items.title: Audit record
items.detail: A stored record of an event. Required event scope and retention are determined by the linked source, not this definition.

sdlc.justification: No differentiating input evidence is provided to favor one lifecycle model over others. The absence of explicit factors such as budget, delivery, failure consequences, feedback, legacy, regulation, schedule, stability, uncertainty, verification, or assurance maturity prevents a ranked selection. All models are equally suitable under current conditions.
tradeoffs: Recurring delivery requires stakeholder review and backlog refinement; a cycle does not guarantee completeness or remove unresolved decisions.
